content:
Your roadmap says what you hope the product does.

Your eval set says what you refuse to ship without.

When a team tells me they have no evals, I ask one question: what must your assistant never say? That list is your first eval. It is also your most honest spec.

Gullwing had 30 stars after two months.

I had written the README last, the way engineers do.

Then I rewrote it first, as if the tool already existed, with three examples you could paste. Stars and issues tripled in a month. I had not changed a line of code.

topic: AI demos only show the happy path
content:
Every AI demo I saw this year answered the question it was built for.

Not one showed a failing conversation.

The failing conversation is the product. What does your team do on Monday when the assistant gets it wrong?

topic: First engineering hire and PR descriptions
content:
I turned down the strongest whiteboard candidate we saw.

His pull request descriptions were one line long. On a three-person team across time zones, writing is the job.

The engineer we hired wrote PRs that explained what he tried and rejected. Most of our onboarding docs started there.

topic: Migration plans are plans for being wrong
content:
We rolled back a nine-month migration in month five.

312 shipments double-counted during a regional outage.

What got us across the line: eight weeks of dual writes and a nightly reconciliation job that paged on any difference. A migration plan is mostly a plan for how you will know it is wrong.
